name: WS2812B 8x8 LED panel (64 pixels)
description: Flexible 8×8 matrix of 64 individually addressable WS2812B RGB LEDs (Worldsemi, 24-bit GRB, 800 kbit/s single-wire data) chained in a zig-zag. Runs on 5 V (3.5–5.3 V); about 60 mA per LED at full white, up to 3.8 A for the whole panel. Sold as: BTF-LIGHTING WS2812B 8x8 64-pixel flexible LED panel (80×80 mm FPC, 3-pin JST-SM input 5V, DIN, GND; matching 5V, DOUT, GND output for chaining).
eli5: A soft square of 64 colour lights you can set one by one, like a tiny screen, using just one data wire.

pins.name: 5V
pins.description: LED supply, 5 V (3.5–5.3 V). Up to 3.8 A at full white: use a separate 5 V supply above low brightness.

pins.name: DIN
pins.description: Data in to the first LED (needs at least 0.7 × the supply voltage as a high; a 300–500 Ω series resistor helps)

buildNotes: Wire the 3-pin JST-SM INPUT connector (5V, DIN, GND printed next to the pads); the output connector (5V, DOUT, GND) on the other side only chains to another panel.

currentMa (420 mA) assumes the driver's default 10 % brightness cap: 64 LEDs × (6 mA + about 0.6 mA idle) at full white. Uncapped full white draws about 3.8 A, more than any board's USB 5 V pin can give: raise brightness only with a separate 5 V 4 A supply whose GND joins the board's GND.
Put a 1000 µF capacitor across 5V and GND at the panel and a 300–500 Ω resistor in series with DIN.
WS2812B wants a data high of at least 0.7 × VDD (3.5 V at 5 V): 3.3 V data usually works on short wires; if the panel flickers, add a 74AHCT125 level shifter.
Never exceed 5.3 V on the panel's supply (datasheet absolute maximum).

driver.code:
# WS2812B 8x8 LED panel (64 pixels), MicroPython helper.
# Uses MicroPython's built-in neopixel module, which produces the WS2812B's
# 800 kbit/s single-wire code (T0H 0.4 us, T1H 0.8 us) and sends each pixel as
# 24 bits in G-R-B order, MSB first, exactly as the Worldsemi datasheet requires.
# A low gap of more than 50 us after write() latches the new colours.
#
# The flexible 8x8 panels are wired in a zig-zag (serpentine): row 0 runs left to
# right from the DIN corner, row 1 runs back right to left, and so on. If your panel
# is wired row-by-row in one direction instead, pass serpentine=False.
#
# brightness scales every colour (0.0-1.0). Each LED draws about 60 mA at full white,
# so the whole panel can pull about 3.8 A at 5 V. The default of 0.1 keeps it near
# 0.4 A, safe on a USB-powered board; raise it only with a separate 5 V supply.
import neopixel


class Matrix8x8:
    WIDTH = 8
    HEIGHT = 8

    def __init__(self, pin, serpentine=True, brightness=0.1):
        self.np = neopixel.NeoPixel(pin, 64)
        self.serpentine = serpentine
        self.brightness = max(0.0, min(1.0, brightness))

    def index(self, x, y):
        """Chain position of the pixel at column x, row y (0,0 = first LED after DIN)."""
        if not (0 <= x < 8 and 0 <= y < 8):
            raise ValueError('x and y must be 0-7')
        if self.serpentine and y & 1:
            x = 7 - x
        return y * 8 + x

    def _scale(self, color):
        b = self.brightness
        return (int(color[0] * b), int(color[1] * b), int(color[2] * b))

    def pixel(self, x, y, color):
        """Set one pixel to color = (r, g, b), 0-255 each. Call show() to send."""
        self.np[self.index(x, y)] = self._scale(color)

    def fill(self, color):
        self.np.fill(self._scale(color))

    def clear(self):
        self.np.fill((0, 0, 0))

    def show(self):
        self.np.write()

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from ws2812b_matrix import Matrix8x8

m = Matrix8x8(Pin({DIN}), brightness=0.1)
m.clear()
m.show()
time.sleep(1)
for y in range(8):
    for x in range(8):
        m.pixel(x, y, (255, 0, 0) if x == y else (0, 0, 255))
m.show()
print('panel lit: red diagonal on blue')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
